messages:
alex: noticing a host-side perf regression on r2 -- p95 decode latency jumped after the last writev change. prospector traces point at request parsing + gRPC small-write overheads.

mai: can you paste the perf numbers?

alex: p50 ~ 24ms -> 28ms, p95 ~ 42ms -> 78ms after commit f2a9b1d. CPU profile shows ~40% of added wall time in host parsing stage and ~20% in streaming writes.

jordan: do we have a flamegraph or flame table?

alex: pasted flame snippet below (reduced):
```
pprof profile.svg
# top stacks by wall-time
- host::parse_request  38.7%
  - host::tokenize 12.1%
  - host::parse_frames 18.3%
- grpc::writev_flush     19.8%
- kvcache::lookup_wait   8.6%
- runtime::kernel_select 6.4%
```

sasha: kv waits bumped too? that feels like election churn on two hot shards. any correlation with kvcache miss rate?

alex: miss rate is steady, but lock contention on hot shard mutex increased. I suspect more small writes caused tighter scheduling and more syscalls -> kernel scheduling jitter.

mai: interesting. two ideas: 1) re-coalesce small frames at ingress (mini-batch window 4ms) to reduce write syscalls; 2) avoid full parse for streaming start tokens (fast-path early-exit).

jordan: +1 for early-exit on short-control-only frames. Also test batching hint to kernel_select: if sequence_len < 32 prefer lightweight kernel to skip KV cache op. Could shave off ~3-4ms.

alex: i'll prototype an ingress coalescer and the fast-path. quick patch:
```patch
- parse_full_frame(data)
+ if likely_control_frame(data): return control_fastpath(data)
+ else: return parse_full_frame(data)
```

sasha: do we have infra to canary that? prefer r2-canary-3.

alex: creating canary now. i'll also add an opt-in flag to enable coalescing window (defaults off).

perfbot: deploybot: canary deploy queued for r2-canary-3 by alex (PR #1427).

mai: when you run the coalescer locally, try these numbers: batch_window_ms=4, max_hold=8, max_coalesced_bytes=8192. See if writev syscall count drops.

jordan: we should measure socket writev counts too: `ss -om` + traced syscalls.

alex: ran local microbench with 10k requests/s: syscall writev count dropped ~62% with batch_window_ms=4, p95 host latency improved from 76ms -> 49ms in the microbench. kv-shard lock time reduced 30%.

sasha: excellent. any regression on tail for long sequences?

alex: negligible for long requests; decode path unaffected. kernel_select hints reduced kernel fallback occurrences by ~12%.

mai: next steps: 1) merge PR behind a runtime flag, 2) canary to r2-canary-3 for 2 hours with perf trace collection, 3) if p95 improvement >20% and no regressions, promote.

jordan: also add a synthetic that targets small frame interleaving (to mimic multiplexed chat). we previously missed that case.

alex: noted. i'll open follow-up to add synthetic and add the pprof baseline dashboard. assigning to self.

perfbot: deploybot: canary deploy succeeded on r2-canary-3 (build f2a9b1d+patch).

sasha: can we get the canary p95 numbers?

alex: canary p95 dropped from 78ms -> 46ms after enabling coalescer (window=4ms). CPU profiles attached to PR. no error increase.

mai: nice. add a short note in the release notes about the opt-in flag and recommended defaults.

jordan: if folks approve, we should consider enabling for Dedicated with a conservative default.

alex: will do. thanks team. leaving the flag off for Hosted until we finish A/B for multi-tenant noise. :thumbsup:
